title: Securities Trading and Disclosure Policy

tiers.name: Directors, officers and employees
tiers.description: All Centaurus directors, officers and employees. Subject to the 30-day no short-term trading rule, the general insider trading prohibition, and (only for those issued options under the Employee Share Option Plan) the ban on arrangements limiting exposure to share price decreases.

tiers.name: Directors and Senior Managers
tiers.description: Directors and Senior Managers (managers reporting directly to the Managing Director). Subject to the additional duty to advise before any proposed transaction, the three blackout periods, and the conditions that trading not be for short-term/speculative gain, not occur while in possession of inside information, and not appear unfair or inappropriate.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors other than the Chairman; must always advise the Chairman prior to any proposed transaction in the Company's securities.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman; must advise the Managing Director and Company Secretary prior to any proposed transaction, and blackout-period exceptional-circumstances trading requires approval of the Chair of the Audit Committee rather than the Chairman.

tiers.name: Senior Managers
tiers.description: Managers who report directly to the Managing Director; must advise the Managing Director and Company Secretary prior to any proposed transaction.

tiers.name: Family or trust/company
tiers.description: A family member, trust or company through which a person included under this policy has influence or control; trading through such a vehicle is barred wherever trading in the person's own name would have been prohibited.

definitions.hedging_definition: arrangements that limit their exposure to losses that would result from share price decreases

windows.start_anchor: 1 week prior to the release of annual and half yearly accounts to the ASX
windows.end_anchor: release of annual and half yearly accounts to the ASX

windows.start_anchor: 1 week prior to the release of the quarterly results announcement to the ASX
windows.end_anchor: release of the quarterly results announcement to the ASX
2 business days after the release of any ASX announcement

rules.detail: 'Securities covered' is limited to securities issued by the Company (shares, preference shares, debentures, options, convertible notes); the policy's operative language is confined to applying for, acquiring or disposing of 'securities of the Company' and does not address a third-party OTC derivative referencing the Company's shares.

rules.section: Policy - Directors and all employees - No arrangements to limit exposure to share price decreases
rules.detail: This express ban is confined to directors, officers and employees who have been issued share options under the Employee Share Option Plan; it does not on its face extend to ordinary shares held outright.
rules.evidence: No director, officer or employee issued with share options under the Company's Employee Share Option Plan shall enter into arrangements that limit their exposure to losses that would result from share price decreases.

rules.detail: The only hedging restriction in the policy applies to Employee Share Option Plan options, not to ordinary vested shares held outright; the policy contains no general hedging definition or dealing definition that would sweep in a hedge of an outright shareholding.
Monetisation transactions (e.g. prepaid forwards) are not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Contracts for difference are not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Margin lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over Company securities is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Secured financing arrangements in respect of Company securities are not mentioned anywhere in the policy.

rules.section: Policy - Directors and all employees - No short-term trading
rules.detail: Absolute ban on trading within a 30 day period; also reflected as a condition for Directors and Senior Managers that trading not be for short-term or speculative gain.
rules.evidence: Centaurus directors, officers and employees must not partake in short-term trading of the Company's securities which is defined as less than a 30 day period.

clearance.evidence: Directors must always advise the Chairman prior to any proposed transaction in the Company's securities.

clearance.evidence: in the case of the Chairman and Senior Managers (means those managers who report directly to the Managing Director), they must advise the Managing Director and Company Secretary.
in the case of the Chairman and Senior Managers (means those managers who report directly to the Managing Director), they must advise the Managing Director and Company Secretary.

short_term.evidence: Centaurus directors, officers and employees must not partake in short-term trading of the Company's securities which is defined as less than a 30 day period.

exceptions.evidence: transfers of securities into a superannuation fund;

exceptions.approver: Board (approves the timing and structure of the offer)
exceptions.evidence: dealing under an offer or invitation made to all or most of Company security holders in the nature of a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board;
the exercise (but not the sale of securities following exercise) of an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme, or the conversion of a convertible security;
any other circumstances determined by the Board.

exceptions.approver: Chairman (or, in the case of the Chairman, the Chair of the Audit Committee)
exceptions.evidence: Trading during blackout periods may only be permitted with prior approval of the Chairman (or, in the case of the Chairman, with the approval of the Chair of the Audit Committee), where there are exceptional circumstances (such as severe financial hardship) and the Director or Senior Manager is not aware of inside information. Where such approval is obtained, trading must occur within 7 days.

exemption_authority: The Chairman (or, for the Chairman, the Chair of the Audit Committee) may approve trading during a blackout period in exceptional circumstances such as severe financial hardship, provided the person is not aware of inside information; approved trading must occur within 7 days. The policy does not address any exemption from the Employee Share Option Plan hedging restriction or the 30-day short-term trading ban.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban confined to ESOP options
bespoke_clauses.clause: No director, officer or employee issued with share options under the Company's Employee Share Option Plan shall enter into arrangements that limit their exposure to losses that would result from share price decreases.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only anti-hedging rule in the policy targets unexercised Employee Share Option Plan options, not ordinary vested shares held outright, so a collar over vested, unencumbered shares falls outside its express wording.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies to all securities issued by the Company from time to time, including ordinary shares, preference shares, debentures, options, convertible notes, etc. ... apply for, acquire, or dispose of securities in the Company
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy's substantive prohibitions are framed around securities issued by the Company and buying/selling them; it does not expressly reach a third-party OTC put/call or a bank loan secured on the shares, so the funded collar structure is not obviously regulated by this document at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (no provision addressing margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance, short selling, stock lending or CFDs appears anywhere in the policy)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the shares is not restricted by this policy, though the company's general disclosure obligations (ASX Listing Rule 3.19A/3.19B notifiable interests) and the standing duty to advise the Chairman would still apply.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Persons included under this policy must not trade through their family or through a trust or company in which they have influence or control, in circumstances where they would have been prohibited in trading in their own name.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or loan cannot be routed through a family member, trust or controlled company to escape a restriction that would otherwise apply to the individual.

bespoke_clauses.clause: 2 business days after the release of any ASX announcement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike the results-specific blackout weeks, this blackout is triggered by any ASX announcement at all, creating frequent short closed windows that could interrupt entry into or unwind of a collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the trading is not likely to be seen by the public, press, other shareholders or ASX to be unfair or inappropriate
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even where a transaction is not expressly prohibited, the Chairman/Managing Director could decline to countenance a collar or secured loan on the subjective ground that it would look unfair or inappropriate to the market.

summary: This is an old (2010/2011), narrowly drafted policy that does not expressly address derivatives, hedging of ordinary shares, margin lending, encumbrance, secured financing, short selling, stock lending or CFDs at all. Its only anti-hedging rule bans directors, officers and employees who hold options under the Employee Share Option Plan from entering into arrangements limiting exposure to share price decreases, and does not extend to ordinary vested shareholdings; because 'Securities covered' and the operative 'buy or sell securities' language are framed around securities issued by the Company, it is doubtful the policy's substantive prohibitions capture an OTC put/call or a bank loan secured on the shares at all. On the facts as drafted, a funded collar over vested, unencumbered shares therefore appears possible, subject to: the general insider trading prohibition; the standing duty for Directors and Senior Managers to always advise the Chairman (or, for the Chairman, the Managing Director and Company Secretary) before any proposed transaction; the three blackout periods (pre-results weeks and 2 business days after any ASX announcement); and the subjective condition that trading not be seen by the public, press, shareholders or ASX as unfair or inappropriate. Given the policy's age and narrow scope, a bank should expect Centaurus to want to give explicit, updated sign-off before proceeding, since the document was not drafted with derivative or secured-financing structures in mind.
